Shoulder and arm trauma foundations: 3

A rugby player lands with the shoulder abducted and externally rotated. The shoulder contour is flattened and imaging shows the head anterior to the glenoid. Which shoulder injury best explains the deformity described?

  1. Acromioclavicular separation
  2. Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation
  3. Anterior shoulder dislocation
  4. Posterior shoulder dislocation
  5. Inferior shoulder dislocation
Answer and explanation

Anterior shoulder dislocation

Anterior glenohumeral displacement often follows abduction and external rotation and places the head anterior to the glenoid.

Option explanations

Anterior shoulder dislocation: Anterior glenohumeral displacement often follows abduction and external rotation and places the head anterior to the glenoid.

Posterior shoulder dislocation: Posterior dislocation may follow seizures or electrical injury and can present with fixed internal rotation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Inferior shoulder dislocation: Luxatio erecta places the humeral head below the glenoid, often with the arm fixed overhead. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Acromioclavicular separation: AC injury disrupts the clavicle-acromion relationship while the humeral head may remain normally located. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Posterior sternoclavicular dislocation: Posterior medial clavicular displacement threatens mediastinal structures and warrants urgent specialist care. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
